body: South of Tsumeb, there's a lush area with completely green grass and mountains.
Near Windhoek, the landscape has dry, rolling hills covered in yellow grass and dead-looking vegetation.
A coastal sandy landscape with some sand dunes is found near Swakopmund, Luderitz, and Oranjemund.
Southeast Namibia has many small, red, sandy ridges oriented NW to SE, creating a bumpy, rollercoaster-like road experience.
Tall, pink sand dunes are a key feature east of Sossusvlei.
Vineyards in Namibia are only found near Aussenkehr, on the southern border with South Africa.
Be aware of some bait-y agricultural fields just west of Mariental.
The A1 between Windhoek and Okahandja is a divided road with a savannah landscape. The only other divided road is near Swakopmund in a coastal desert setting.
The B1 south of Grunau is a desolate, paved road heading N-NE through a desert with sparse, dry vegetation.

The B1 is missing its outer yellow lines in three sections: a hilly, poor-quality stretch between Grunau and Keetmanshoop; a cloudy part north of Keetmanshoop; and a flat, N-NE section between Gibeon and Mariental.
Between Gibeon and Tses, the road has wider shoulders and excellent pavement quality.
The B1 between Mariental and Rehoboth has an arid steppe landscape and a distinct NW road angle.
Approaching Windhoek from Rehoboth, the landscape becomes greener with more prominent, pointed hills.
North of Okahandja, the B1 is flat with a northbound direction and a bright sun to the N-NW. Look for two pointy mountains west of the road south of Sukses.
The B2 NE of Swakopmund has sandy soil and a mountain ridge to the east. Closer to Swakopmund, the sky is hazy.
Between Karibib and Usakos, you'll find sunrise coverage with thin clouds and mountains to the north.
East of Karibib, the weather is clear, and the road has wide shoulder lines with an E-NE angle.
This desolate paved road heads E-SE through a flat, dry landscape with small clouds. The shrubbery is quite green, especially in the hilly eastern part.
The B4 east of Luderitz features bright, sandy soil and a nearby railway to the south.
East of Aus, the road winds through table-topped mountains with a railway to the south.
East of Kuibis, the road is on a mostly flat plateau with very red soil.
Between Seeheim and Keetmanshoop, the landscape is flat with mountains always nearby.
Road B6 east from Windhoek has a landscape that varies from hilly to flat, with orange-tinged soil and cloudy skies.
This long stretch of the B8 is recognizable by its light-colored, grainy pavement and general E-NE direction.
This paved, N-NW bound road has bright soil and a tabletop mountain ridge to the east under a clear sky.
The C14 is an unpaved road with a cloudy sky, especially in the northern half. The southern end is paved and has a clear sky.
The paved C19 is recognizable by its very red soil and small tufts of golden grass, under a mostly dark, cloudy sky.
The C22 is a paved road heading east with freshly cut, orange grass tufts along the side. The sun is low to the east.
A large, rugged mountain formation is visible to the west from the paved C13. Look for wispy clouds near the sun in the east.
The C34 looks like streaks of black sand on sand. Look for unique white bollards with yellow and red reflectors.
The northern section of road C35 has red-tinted pavement and a green, grassy landscape with low-lying cumulus clouds.
South of the C41 intersection, the C35 loses its red pavement and the quality worsens. The landscape is sandy and hilly, with a consistent S-SE direction.
A section of road NW of Kamanjab has a green, hilly landscape with impressive clouds and orange hues on the horizon at sunset.
A very rugged mountain formation can be seen to the west from a few sections of the C35 and its side roads.
The C38 is a paved northern road with a spotty blanket of clouds being its most distinct feature.
The C39 runs through a wide valley with small, vegetation-covered hills, especially to the north.
The C40 has a general NW angle through flat terrain. Closer to Kamanjab, the sun sets to the west.
East of the C35 intersection, this road has a constant SW to NW angle and grainy pavement. West of the intersection, the landscape is much hillier.
Along the C43, you can find some of the most impressive red-colored tabletop mountains.
The C44 is a wide, unpaved, sandy road with a general E-SE angle and a westbound driving direction.
The C47 is an even wider unpaved road than the C44, with slightly redder soil. The driving direction is SW.
The C49 in the panhandle often has poor quality pavement with only white road lines or no lines at all.

The D3600 and the unlabelled road going NE to Mpungu, have a very light coloured, sometimes grainy pavement, with at times very faded yellow lines, which are hard to even see. Combined with the either exactly N to S or NE angle, as well as the northern landscape, make this road very distinct.

A few roads in the north lack the typical outer yellows. The C46, which is a long road going generally NW to SE. The E-W section by Ruacana, has very poor pavement. SE of Oshikuku, the sun is low in the sky to the NW. C41 (M123) also has a NW angle but has more clouds in the sky than the C46. B10 west of Eenhana is an E-W stretch, which is more vegetated, and also has the sun low in the sky to the west. B10 east of Nkurenkuru is another NW bound stretch with the sun low in the sky, but this part is much more vegetated than the C46. You can also see the moon to the east. D3615 is a short road with a constant N-NE angle that technically has outer yellows, but they are quite faded.

Windhoek is by far the largest city in Namibia, as well as the richest, with many high rise buildings near downtown. Affluent and often gated single family houses are a common sight on the sides of hilly streets, which are often well marked with simple white street signs. In the northwest of the city you’ll find the slums dotting the hills.

Gobabis is a big north-south gridded city in the desert, with red soil permeating the landscape and roads, which are very often unpaved. A faint green ridge is sometimes visible to the north to northwest. The street signs, while rare, are also green, with silver framing on the top and bottom. Blue bins are also a good clue for Gobabis.

The coastal cities of Swakopmund and Walvis Bay are flat and often have sandy streets, with palms and Norfolk pines planted around. Street and road signs often have square-shaped signposts. Road angles can be used to line up parts of the city, but a northeast bound angle is common in both. These white and blue plastic containers are common in Swakopmund, as are yellow lamp posts in downtown areas.

While very similar to Swakopmund and Walvis Bay, Henties Bay is less gridded and noticeably poorer, with most roads being unpaved. Unlike in Swakopmund, where yellow lamps are only found near the downtown, here they can occasionally be found throughout the town. The cloudy weather can be used to confirm the town.
Longstrand is a small resort town between Swakopmund and Walvis Bay with pink brick sidewalks next to essentially every road. The weather is always overcast and gloomy.
Light coloured rocky hillsides are everywhere in the hilly coastal town of Luderitz.

Oranjemund is a well-off gridded city with almost exactly east to west streets, with an abundance of planted vegetation all around the city. Multiple Norfolk pines can be seen almost everywhere. Streets are well organised with E-W avenues and N-S streets, which can be seen written on small blue markers next to the gates or on street signs, which have varying designs.
Orange coloured thatched fences, walls, and huts are everywhere in the desert town of Aussenkehr, which is built on the slope of a hill.

While not as common, the same thatched architecture is present in Noordoewer, and unlike Aussenkehr, the town was built on flat land, with an imposing cliffside visible to the southwest, across the border in South Africa. Similar mountains can be seen to the north as well.
Rosh Pinah can easily be recognised by the dry mountains just northeast of the city, as well as slightly further away to the southwest.
The landscape of Aus is very rocky, with dry hills devoid of vegetation all around. The hills to the north have a fairly smooth sloped shape, while the peaks to the south are more rugged.
While not entirely unique, most streets in Rundu consist of deep and light coloured sand, with a bumpy texture, and tire tracks engraved into it.
Orange coloured mountains, which are covered in green vegetation surround the partly hilly town of Opuwo, from where you have a great vantage point of the mountains.

Otavi sits in between many sets of mountains, all of which are quite far away, but can be seen from the city. Being a northern town, Otavi is quite green, with slightly reddish sandy soil, which is common for the more northern cities. The entire town is on a northeast to southwest grid, which can rule out similar looking cities like Grootfontein and Tsumeb.
From almost anywhere in Karibib the dark silhouette of Erongo Mountain can be seen to the north. Dry hills covered in shrubbery flank the town to the south.

A lone tall ridge with a rugged, striated texture lies to the SSE of Usakos. Another smaller plain textured mountain, which has a red tint to it, is just to the east, or northeast, depending on part of town. From the northern part of town, the cliffy edges of Erongo Mountain are visible to the north.

The crown-like outline of Mt Brandeburg is barely visible to the northwest from most parts of Uis, while Many other dry hills surround the town. The open pit mines, which have a distinctive white colour, can be seen from the western half of Uis.

Ariamsvlei can be recognised by a single flat-topped hill with rocky ridgelines near the top, and small amounts of green shrubbery dotting the slopes. The hill is either to the north, or east, depending on the part of town. The soil has a dark red tint to it, with lots of bushes and small trees growing around the place.
